name: Revenge of Gann
summary: In the southern Barrens, Gann Stonespire prepares to strike back at the Bael Modan dwarves. After Prospector Khazgorm's death, he sends Horde allies into the fortress for volatile munitions to fuel his attack.

sections.title: A Taste of Their Own Medicine
sections.body: Gann Stonespire knows Prospector Khazgorm's death only slowed the Bael Modan dig site. Dwarven work will resume, and another foreman will soon oversee the machines tearing through Gann's ancestral land. He refuses to watch the earth suffer more excavation. Instead, Gann plans to turn the invaders' demolitions gear against them and rupture their stronghold from within.

sections.title: Raiding the Keep
sections.body: Bael Modan's fortress holds an excavation base and a garrison of soldiers, riflemen, and officers protecting dwarven interests in the Barrens. Gann has learned that its defenders carry nitroglycerin, wood pulp, and sodium nitrate, materials used in industrial demolition. He sends Horde allies past the perimeter to take these volatile supplies from the dwarves. With enough gathered, he can assemble a powerful satchel charge.

faq.q: Why is Gann Stonespire seeking revenge?
aliases: what did dwarves do to gann
faq.answer: The Ironforge dwarves at Bael Modan overran Gann's ancestral homeland, desecrated the soil, and drove his people out to establish their excavation site. After killing the chief prospector and recovering his journal, Gann seeks to stop the destruction for good.

faq.q: Where are the explosive materials found?
faq.answer: Bael Modan's defenders carry the ingredients. Riflemen, soldiers, and officers within and around the fortified dig site in the southern Barrens have nitroglycerin vials, wood pulp bundles, and sodium nitrate samples.

faq.q: Why does Gann need wood pulp and chemicals?
faq.answer: Dwarven excavation schematics show that wood pulp stabilizes volatile nitroglycerin, while sodium nitrate helps make a reliable industrial explosive. Gann plans to shape the mixture into a demolitions charge that can bring down key dwarven structures.

faq.q: What happens after gathering the supplies?
faq.answer: When you return the raw components, Gann assembles an explosive charge and sends you to destroy the dwarves' flying machine at the Bael Modan excavation, a key part of the site's infrastructure.

faq.q: Why doesn't slaying Khazgorm end the dwarven threat?
faq.answer: Khazgorm was only the lead prospector. Bael Modan's dwarven forces are entrenched behind defensive walls and supply lines, and Ironforge can send another foreman to continue digging unless the base suffers a catastrophic blow.

faq.q: What is Bael Modan's strategic threat to the Horde?
aliases: why horde care about bael modan
faq.answer: Bael Modan began as a keep defending the dig site, but it has grown into a heavily manned Alliance stronghold. Its position along the southern Barrens trade routes makes it a military threat to nearby Horde settlements in Kalimdor.

angles.text: As a tauren, you can see Bael Modan as a grievous wound against the Earth Mother. Sabotaging the dwarven machinery is a duty to your spirit and homeland.
As a member of the Horde, you help keep the Alliance from establishing a military foothold in the southern Barrens that could sever travel between Mulgore, Crossroads, and the southern frontier.
As an engineer, you recognize the classic dwarven industrial formula: nitroglycerin stabilized with pulp and mixed with sodium nitrate. Gann adapts it for an uneven fight.
